What happens to my Discord when I die?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 26 Oct 2026

Short answer: Discord won't give anyone access to a deceased person's account or share its data, and it has no memorialise or transfer option. Family can ask Discord Support to delete the account: write from the account's own email, or send proof of death, proof of relationship and photo ID. Accounts unused for 2 years or more may be deleted automatically.

Key facts

  • No account access or data for family
  • No memorialise or transfer option
  • Deletion on request with documents
  • Unused for 2+ years: may be deleted automatically

How do I prepare my Discord account?

  1. Keep the email address linked to your Discord account in a password manager with emergency access. Discord says whoever controls that email can reset the password.
  2. Write your Discord username and your wishes (delete or leave it) in your digital estate plan.
  3. After a death, with access to the account: User Settings, My Account, Account Removal, Delete Account, then enter the password.
  4. Writing from the account's own email: send Discord Support the sentence "I confirm that I would like to delete the account associated with [email]."
  5. Writing from another email: send the account email and username, a death certificate or coroner's report, proof of relationship and your photo ID, plus "I request to have the account associated with [email and/or username] deleted."
  6. Billing questions (such as Nitro): use Discord's support form and choose Billing.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • The account's email address and Discord username
  • From another email: death certificate or coroner's report
  • Proof of relationship: marriage licence, birth certificate, will, estate letter or power of attorney
  • Your valid photo ID or passport (scans or photocopies; you can black out birthdays and addresses but keep names visible)

How long does it take?

Discord publishes no processing time for deletion requests. Accounts not used for 2 years or more may be scheduled for deletion, and the deletion proceeds automatically as long as no one logs in.

What can't be recovered?

  • Messages and data in the account, because Discord doesn't release them to family
  • Everything in the account once it's deleted

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my Discord when I die?

Discord won't give anyone access to a deceased person's account or share its data, and it has no memorialise or transfer option. Family can ask Discord Support to delete the account: write from the account's own email, or send proof of death, proof of relationship and photo ID. Accounts unused for 2 years or more may be deleted automatically.

Can family get into a dead person's Discord account?

Discord says it can't provide access, share data or make changes. Whoever has the account's email can reset the password, but check with the executor before using it.

Does Discord memorialise accounts?

No. Discord says it doesn't currently have a feature to memorialise or transfer accounts.

How do I delete a deceased person's Discord account?

Delete it from User Settings if you can sign in, or contact Discord Support. From another email, include the account email and username, a death certificate, proof of relationship, your photo ID and an explicit deletion statement.

Do inactive Discord accounts get deleted?

Discord says accounts unused for 2 years or more may be scheduled for deletion, with a warning sent to the account's email or phone first.
